app_title.context: Name of the app, shown at the top of the page: this language's ordinary word for a report, as a name. The app turns a short request into a financial report of a Bkper Book. One short noun.

app_loading.context: Shown with a spinner while the app signs the person in and loads their Books, before anything else can show. Short, ends with an ellipsis.

input_label.context: Accessible label of the single text input where the person describes, in their own words, the financial report they want. Short noun phrase.

input_placeholder.text: Describe a report, like expenses by month this year
input_placeholder.context: Placeholder text inside the empty report input. The report builds itself as the person types, with no submit button. The example is a typical request: the expenses of the Book, month by month, in the current year. Keep it short and lowercase after the first word, without ending punctuation.

completion_label.context: Accessible name of the short list that opens above the report request input while the person types, offering the names of the Book's groups and accounts that complete the word being typed. Choosing one writes that exact name into the request. Short noun phrase.

completion_group.context: Small tag beside a name in the list that completes the word typed in the report request: this name is a Group of the Book, not an Account. One word, a noun.

completion_account.context: Small tag beside a name in the list that completes the word typed in the report request: this name is an Account of the Book, not a Group. One word, a noun.

suggestions_label.context: Accessible label of the list of three suggested reports shown under the empty input. Clicking one builds that report. One short noun.

suggestions_loading.context: Message announced to screen readers while the three suggested reports of the Book load, under the empty input. Short, ends with an ellipsis.

status_loading.context: Message announced to screen readers while a report is being built from the Book's balances. Short, ends with an ellipsis.

hint_not_a_report.text: That doesn't look like a report of this Book. Name a group and a period, or pick a suggestion.
hint_not_a_report.context: Quiet hint shown under the input when the request could not be understood as a report of the Book. A group is a Bkper Group, such as Expenses or Assets; a period is a time range, such as this year or October. Friendly, two short sentences.

book_picker_title.context: Heading of the list of the person's recent Books, shown when the app opens without a Book. A Book is a Bkper ledger. Short imperative.

book_picker_empty.context: Shown in place of the Book list when the person has no Books. A Book is a Bkper ledger.

book_picker_filter.context: Placeholder and accessible label of the search field above the list of the person's recent Books; typing filters all their Books by name. A Book is a Bkper ledger. Short imperative, without ending punctuation.

book_picker_no_match.context: Shown in place of the Book list when no Book name contains the words typed in the search field. A Book is a Bkper ledger. Short.

book_untitled.context: Name shown in the Book list for a Book that has no name. A Book is a Bkper ledger. Short noun phrase.

books_back.context: Small button at the top of a Book's report page that goes back to the list of the person's Books. A Book is a Bkper ledger. One short word.

sign_in.context: Button that signs the person in to Bkper so the app can read their Books. Short imperative.

retry.context: Button shown with an error message; it repeats the request that failed. Short imperative.

error_book_not_found.text: This Book was not found, or you can't access it.
error_book_not_found.context: Error shown when the Book in the address does not exist or is not shared with the person. A Book is a Bkper ledger.

error_forbidden.text: You don't have permission to read this Book.
error_forbidden.context: Error shown when the person may not read the balances of the Book. A Book is a Bkper ledger.

error_ai_allowance_exhausted.text: Your Bkper AI allowance is used up. You can still pick a suggestion.
error_ai_allowance_exhausted.context: Error shown when the person's monthly Bkper AI usage allowance has run out, so typed requests cannot be understood. Suggested reports still work because they need no AI. Keep the product name Bkper AI unchanged.

error_upstream.text: Bkper didn't respond. Try again in a moment.
error_upstream.context: Error shown when Bkper's servers failed to answer while the report was being built. Keep the name Bkper unchanged.

error_unexpected.context: Generic error shown when the report failed for an unknown reason.

error_load_data.text: Couldn't load your Books. Reload the page to try again.
error_load_data.context: Error shown when the app opens and cannot sign the person in or load their list of Books. A Book is a Bkper ledger. Two short sentences.

error_book_load.context: Error shown at the top of a Book's report page when the Book's name and details could not be loaded. A Book is a Bkper ledger. Short.

error_future_period.context: Error shown when the request asks for a period in the future, such as next year, which has no balances yet.

error_no_net_result.text: This Book has no group that combines income and expenses. Add one in Bkper to see its net result.
error_no_net_result.context: Error shown when the person asks for the net result (income minus expenses) of a Book whose groups give none: no Bkper Group holds both its Incoming and its Outgoing groups, and Report does not calculate one from its other groups. The second sentence suggests creating such a Group in Bkper.

error_no_activity_roots.text: This Book has no income or expense groups for a net result.
error_no_activity_roots.context: Error shown when a net result (income minus expenses, profit and loss) is requested but the Book has no top-level Groups of Incoming or Outgoing Accounts. A Book is a Bkper ledger.

error_unknown_root.text: That group isn't a top-level group of this Book.
error_unknown_root.context: Error shown when a report asks for a Group that is not a top-level (root) Group of the Book. Reports start at a top-level Group, such as Expenses or Assets.

error_unknown_target.text: That group or account is no longer where this report found it in the Book.
error_unknown_target.context: Error shown when a saved or shared report names a Group or Account of the Book that was deleted, or moved out of the top-level Group the report reads it from. A Book is a Bkper ledger. One short sentence.

error_mixed_targets.text: Balances of assets or liabilities can't be side by side with income or expenses. Ask for them in separate reports.
error_mixed_targets.context: Error shown when a report asks for several Groups or Accounts side by side, but some are of Asset or Liability Accounts (balances at a date) and others of Incoming or Outgoing Accounts (income or expenses within a period), which cannot be shown together. A Book is a Bkper ledger. Two short sentences.

report_net_result.context: Title of the report of income minus expenses over a period: all Incoming Accounts minus all Outgoing Accounts (profit and loss). Also labels its total amount. Short noun phrase, title or sentence case as the language uses.

report_document_title.context: Title of the browser tab or file of a report: the report's title, a middle dot, then the Book's name. Keep the separator and both placeholders.

placeholders.report: title of the report: the name of a Group of the Book, verbatim, or the translated words Net result

period_all.context: Period of a report: every date from the Book's first transaction up to today, the whole history of the Book. Shown under the report title, standing alone, as a period name such as all time or since the beginning.

period_quarter.context: A calendar quarter of a year, as a compact label, such as Q3 2026 for July to September 2026. Use the language's usual short form for a quarter.

placeholders.year: the year, in digits, such as 2026

position_as_of.context: Date of a balance report (the amounts of Assets or Liabilities at the end of a day), shown under the report title, such as As of Dec 31, 2026: the usual accounting phrase for the date of a balance sheet, not until or since.

placeholders.date: the date, already formatted in the language, such as Dec 31, 2026

request_year_to_date.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. The period from the start of the current year through the current month, as in Expenses year to date.

request_year_to_date_in_year.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. The months from the start of another year through the same month as today's, as in Expenses year to date last year, or Expenses year to date 2024. Never repeat a word: the year may be said in words that end the phrase the same way, such as last year.

placeholders.year: a year in digits (2024) or relative to today (last year, 2 years ago), already in the language

request_last_12_months.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. The 12 months through the current month, as in Expenses last 12 months.

request_all_time.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. The whole history of the Book, every date up to today, as in Expenses all time.

request_quarter.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. A calendar quarter named without its year, such as Q3 for July to September. Write it as a person types a quarter so that it cannot be read as anything else, such as Q3 in English or 3º trimestre in Portuguese, where a bare letter and number (T3) is not read as a quarter; the same form as in a quarter with its year in a request.

request_quarter_in_year.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. A calendar quarter of a year written in digits, such as Q3 2024 for July to September 2024. Write the quarter as in a quarter named without its year, such as Q3 in English or 3º trimestre in Portuguese, so that it cannot be read as anything else.

placeholders.year: the year, in digits, such as 2024

request_in_year.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. A period within a year: a month, a quarter, year to date or this month, then a year that is either written in digits or said relative to today, such as January last year, Q1 this year or year to date 2024. Add a word between them only where the language needs one, and keep both placeholders.

placeholders.period: a month (January), a quarter (Q1), year to date, or this month or last month, already in the language
placeholders.year: a year in digits (2024) or relative to today (this year, last year, 2 years ago), already in the language

request_year_earlier.text: the same period a year earlier
request_year_earlier.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. What a period is compared with: the same months one year before, as in Expenses this quarter vs. the same period a year earlier. Short noun phrase.

request_same_month.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. What a month is compared with: the same month of the year that follows it, written in digits or said relative to today, as in Expenses last month vs. the same month last year, or Expenses this month vs. the same month 2023. Short noun phrase.

request_same_quarter.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. What a quarter of a year is compared with: the same quarter of the year that follows it, written in digits or said relative to today, as in Expenses this quarter vs. the same quarter last year. Short noun phrase.

request_same_months.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. What a run of months, such as year to date or the last 12 months, is compared with: the same months of the year that follows it, written in digits or said relative to today, as in Expenses year to date vs. the same months last year. Short noun phrase.

request_versus.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it, after the report's title (the name of a Group, such as Expenses). Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. A period compared with another, as in Revenue last year vs. 2023 or Expenses Q3 vs. Q1. Write the connective a person would type to ask for a comparison, keeping both placeholders; the order may change as the language needs.

placeholders.period: the period of the report, already in the language, such as last year or Q3
placeholders.compared: the period it is compared with, already in the language, such as 2023, Q1 or the same period a year earlier

request_by_month.context: Part of the request a report stands for, written into the app's input when a report is opened from a link and sent to the decision model when the person edits it, so it must read as a person would type it. Write it as typed, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation. A report shown month by month: what the report is of, then how it is shown, followed in the request by its period, as in Expenses by month this year or Expenses by month last 12 months. Write the words a person types to ask for amounts month by month, keeping the name apart from them with a space where the language allows.

placeholders.name: what the report is of: the name of a Group or Account of the Book, verbatim, the names of several Groups or Accounts joined as a list, or the translated words Net result

notice_comparison_fallback.text: The comparison asked for isn’t an earlier period of the same kind, so this compares with {period}.
notice_comparison_fallback.context: Note under a report's title when the request compared its period with another that cannot be compared: a period of another kind (a month for a year) or one that is not earlier (it overlaps). The report then compares with the period right before instead, named in the placeholder. One short sentence.

placeholders.period: the period the report compares with instead, already formatted, such as 2024, Q2 2026, October 2026 or Oct 31, 2026

notice_comparison_none.text: All time has nothing before it to compare with, so nothing is compared.
notice_comparison_none.context: Note under a report's title when the request compared the whole history of the Book (all time) with another period: there is nothing earlier, so the report shows no comparison. One short sentence.

notice_chart_unfit.context: Note under a report's title when the person asked for a chart that cannot show the report's numbers honestly: the report shows the closest chart that fits instead. Names the chart asked for, then why it is not shown. One short line.

placeholders.chart: the short name of the chart asked for, already translated, as under its small preview, such as Donut, Stacked or By month
placeholders.reason: why it is not shown, already translated, a short sentence without ending punctuation, such as Taxes is below zero (-186.74)

answer_compared_with.context: Shown next to the percentage change of a report's amount, naming what it is compared with: the previous period, such as vs. 2025 or vs. Q2 2026, or an earlier date for a balance. Very short.

placeholders.period: the earlier period or date, already formatted, such as 2025, Q2 2026, October 2026 or Jan 1 – Nov 5, 2025

chart_by_month.context: Accessible label of a chart showing a report's amount in each month of the period.

placeholders.name: title of the report: the name of a Group of the Book, verbatim, the names of several Groups or Accounts joined as a list, or the translated words Net result

chart_breakdown.context: Accessible label of a chart comparing the parts (sub-groups and Accounts) of a report's amount.

placeholders.name: title of the report: the name of a Group of the Book, verbatim, or the translated words Net result

chart_side_by_side.context: Accessible label of a chart or table showing several Groups or Accounts of the Book next to each other, each with its own amount, never added up.

placeholders.names: names of the Groups or Accounts, verbatim, already joined as a list in the language, such as Food and Rent

charts_label.context: Accessible label of the row of small chart previews under a report's chart: every chart that fits the report, to show it another way. Read by screen readers, not shown.

chart_name_bar.context: Short name of a chart, under a small preview of it that the person clicks to show the report as that chart. One or two words; keep it as short as possible. This one: bars of the report's amount in each month.

chart_name_line.context: Short name of a chart, under a small preview of it that the person clicks to show the report as that chart. One or two words; keep it as short as possible. This one: a line of a balance at the end of each month.

chart_name_area.context: Short name of a chart, under a small preview of it that the person clicks to show the report as that chart. One or two words; keep it as short as possible. This one: an area chart, the amounts of each month filled down to zero.

chart_name_stacked.context: Short name of a chart, under a small preview of it that the person clicks to show the report as that chart. One or two words; keep it as short as possible. This one: stacked bars, the parts of the amount piled up in each month.

chart_name_ranked_bar.context: Short name of a chart, under a small preview of it that the person clicks to show the report as that chart. One or two words; keep it as short as possible. This one: horizontal bars of the parts of the amount, largest first.

chart_name_donut.context: Short name of a chart, under a small preview of it that the person clicks to show the report as that chart. One or two words; keep it as short as possible. This one: a donut chart (a ring) of each part's share of the total.

chart_name_compare.context: Short name of a chart, under a small preview of it that the person clicks to show the report as that chart. One or two words; keep it as short as possible. This one: each part in this period beside the same part in the previous period.

chart_name_waterfall.context: Short name of a chart, under a small preview of it that the person clicks to show the report as that chart. One or two words; keep it as short as possible. This one: a waterfall (bridge) chart, from a starting amount step by step to the final amount.

chart_name_table.context: Short name of a chart, under a small preview of it that the person clicks to show the report as that chart. One or two words; keep it as short as possible. This one: no chart at all, only the table of numbers under it.

chart_unfit_negative_part.context: Why the donut chart the person asked for is not shown: one of its parts is below zero, and a slice cannot be negative. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

placeholders.name: the name of a Group or Account of the Book, verbatim, such as Taxes
placeholders.amount: its amount, already formatted in the language, with its minus sign, such as -186.74

chart_unfit_mixed_parts.text: The parts are of different types
chart_unfit_mixed_parts.context: Why the donut chart the person asked for is not shown: its parts are of different Bkper types (such as Assets and Liabilities, or Incoming and Outgoing), so they are not slices of one whole. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_stacked_mixed_parts.text: Parts of different types don't stack up
chart_unfit_stacked_mixed_parts.context: Why the stacked bar chart the person asked for is not shown: the parts are of different Bkper types (such as Assets and Liabilities), so piling them up makes no total. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_net_result.text: Income and expenses aren't slices of a net result
chart_unfit_net_result.context: Why the donut chart the person asked for is not shown: the report is a net result (income minus expenses), which is not a whole made of slices. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_stacked_net_result.text: Income and expenses don't stack up to a net result
chart_unfit_stacked_net_result.context: Why the stacked bar chart the person asked for is not shown: a net result is income minus expenses, so piling them up does not make it. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_few_parts.text: There are fewer than two parts to show
chart_unfit_few_parts.context: Why the chart the person asked for is not shown: the report's amount has fewer than two parts (sub-Groups or Accounts) with an amount. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_too_many_parts.text: There are too many parts for a donut
chart_unfit_too_many_parts.context: Why the donut chart the person asked for is not shown: more parts than a donut can show clearly. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_stacked_too_many_parts.text: There are too many parts to stack
chart_unfit_stacked_too_many_parts.context: Why the stacked bar chart the person asked for is not shown: the amount has more parts (Groups or Accounts) than stacked bars draw, each of its own. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_few_months.text: The period has fewer than two months
chart_unfit_few_months.context: Why the chart over time the person asked for is not shown: the report's period covers fewer than two months. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_no_amounts.text: There are no amounts to show
chart_unfit_no_amounts.context: Why the chart the person asked for is not shown: every amount it would draw is zero. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_no_previous.text: There is no earlier period to compare with
chart_unfit_no_previous.context: Why the comparison or bridge chart the person asked for is not shown: the report has no previous period, as when it covers all time. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_not_a_whole.text: The parts don't add up to the total
chart_unfit_not_a_whole.context: Why the donut or stacked bar chart the person asked for is not shown: the parts Bkper lists (Groups or Accounts) do not add up to the Group's own total, so they cannot be shown as slices of it. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_no_bridge.text: A bridge would show amounts that aren't Bkper balances
chart_unfit_no_bridge.context: Why the bridge (waterfall) chart the person asked for is not shown: Report shows only balances that Bkper calculates, and the bars of a bridge would be sums Report makes itself. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

chart_unfit_side_by_side.text: Side by side, they aren't parts of one total
chart_unfit_side_by_side.context: Why the donut or stacked bar chart the person asked for is not shown: the report shows several Groups or Accounts side by side, each with its own amount, and they are not slices of one total. Shown in a note under the report's title, after Can’t show and the chart's name. No ending punctuation.

breakdown_label.context: Accessible label of the table listing the parts of a report's amount: its sub-groups and Accounts, each with its amount, share and change. One short noun.

breakdown_column_name.context: Column header of the breakdown table: the name of each Group or Account. One short word.

breakdown_column_amount.context: Column header of the breakdown table: the money amount of each Group or Account in the period. One short word.

breakdown_column_share.context: Column header of the breakdown table: each row's share of its parent's amount, as a percentage (a share of the total, not a quota or an allowance). One short word.

breakdown_column_change.context: Column header of the breakdown table: the percentage change of each row's amount from the previous period. One short word.

breakdown_column_trend.context: Column header of the breakdown table: a small line chart of each row's amount month by month. Very short.

breakdown_expand.context: Accessible label of the control that opens a row of the breakdown table to show its sub-groups and Accounts. Short imperative.

breakdown_collapse.context: Accessible label of the control that closes an open row of the breakdown table, hiding its sub-groups and Accounts. Short imperative.

breakdown_empty.context: Shown in place of the breakdown table when no Account of the report has an amount in the period.

source_label.context: Heading of the section at the end of a report that states where its numbers come from: the Book, the period, the exact Bkper query and when the balances were read. One short noun.

source_details.context: Button on the line at the end of a report, opposite the link 'Open in Bkper', that shows or hides where the report's numbers come from: its exact dates, the Bkper query, when the balances were read and the Book. One short noun, as on a disclosure control; not an imperative.

source_footer.context: Sentence at the end of a report stating that every number was computed from the balances of the named Book. A Book is a Bkper ledger.

source_calculated.context: Label in the source notes at the end of a report: the net result (income minus expenses) shown was calculated by the Report app, not by Bkper. Report is the app's name. Short.

source_calculated_note.text: Incoming groups minus Outgoing groups. Add a group that holds both, and Bkper calculates the net result.
source_calculated_note.context: Note after the label 'Calculated by Report' at the end of a report: how the app calculated the net result, from the Book's top-level Incoming and Outgoing Groups, and a suggestion to create a Bkper Group that holds both, so Bkper calculates the net result itself. Incoming and Outgoing are Bkper account types.

source_period.context: Label of the exact dates the report covers, in the source section at the end of a report. One short noun.

source_query.context: Label of the exact Bkper search query whose transactions the report sums, in the source section at the end of a report. One short noun.

source_data_at.context: Label of the date and time the report's balances were read from Bkper, in the source section at the end of a report. Short phrase.

source_open_in_bkper.context: Link that opens the report's query in the Book in Bkper, to see the transactions behind the numbers. Keep the name Bkper unchanged. Short imperative.

source_open_in_report.context: Link at the end of a report file that opens the same report in the Report app, where it can be changed. Report is the app's name, shown at the top of its page: write it as this language's ordinary word for a report, as a name. Short imperative.

suggestion_breakdown_this_year.context: Suggested report, shown as an example request: the amount of a Group in the current year, with its parts. Write it as the person would type it, lowercase where the language allows, no ending punctuation.

placeholders.root: name of a Group of the Book, verbatim, such as Expenses

suggestion_breakdown_year.context: Suggested report, shown as an example request: the amount of a Group in a past year, with its parts. Write it as the person would type it, no ending punctuation.

placeholders.root: name of a Group of the Book, verbatim, such as Expenses
placeholders.year: a year in digits, such as 2019

suggestion_monthly_this_year.context: Suggested report, shown as an example request: the amount of a Group in each month of the current year. Write it as the person would type it, no ending punctuation.

placeholders.root: name of a Group of the Book, verbatim, such as Expenses

suggestion_monthly_year.context: Suggested report, shown as an example request: the amount of a Group in each month of a past year. Write it as the person would type it, no ending punctuation.

placeholders.root: name of a Group of the Book, verbatim, such as Expenses
placeholders.year: a year in digits, such as 2019

suggestion_position_today.context: Suggested report, shown as an example request: the balance today of a Group of Assets or Liabilities, such as Bank accounts. Write it as the person would type it, no ending punctuation.

placeholders.root: name of a Group of the Book, verbatim, such as Assets

suggestion_position_year_end.context: Suggested report, shown as an example request: the balance of a Group of Assets or Liabilities on the last day of a past year. Write it as the person would type it, no ending punctuation.

placeholders.root: name of a Group of the Book, verbatim, such as Assets
placeholders.year: a year in digits, such as 2019

suggestion_net_result_this_year.context: Suggested report, shown as an example request: income minus expenses (profit and loss) in the current year. Write it as the person would type it, no ending punctuation.

suggestion_net_result_year.context: Suggested report, shown as an example request: income minus expenses (profit and loss) in a past year. Write it as the person would type it, no ending punctuation.

placeholders.year: a year in digits, such as 2019

shelf_access_error.text: Saved reports access changed. Reload to check access.
shelf_access_error.context: Alert under the Book-shared shelf when the server denies a shelf read or mutation, authentication expires, or the Book is not found. Reload saved reports checks current access. Never imply the client can grant permission.

shelf_label.context: Accessible name of the horizontally scrolling Book-shared prompt shelf just above the request input. Prompts are requests rerun freshly, not stored report data.

shelf_load_error.text: Saved reports could not load. Try reloading.
shelf_load_error.context: Alert under the Book-shared shelf after a list/storage/network failure. The report and request input remain usable. Reload saved reports is available.

shelf_loading.context: Quiet status below the Book-shared prompt shelf while its list and permissions load. Keep short.

shelf_reload.context: Recovery action under the Book-shared shelf after a list or mutation failure. Fetches the list and fresh server permissions. Does not run a report.

shelf_remove.context: Item of the small menu of one Book-shared saved request, in the row of saved requests just above the report request input. Removes the saved request from the row for everyone in the Book; never removes financial data or reports. Short imperative.

shelf_remove_error.text: Could not remove the saved request. Try removing it again.
shelf_remove_error.context: Alert under the Book-shared shelf after a removal fails. The saved item remains visible with its remove control so the person can retry safely.

shelf_save.context: One-click action beside the prompt shelf. Saves the successfully shown report’s original request for everyone in this Book, not report data or later draft input. Keep very short.

shelf_save_error.text: Could not save this request. Try Save again.
shelf_save_error.context: Alert under the Book-shared shelf after saving the shown report’s original request fails. Retrying the Save button is safe; no prompt or upstream details are shown.

shelf_save_label.context: Accessible name of the one-click Save action beside the shelf. Names the actual original request being saved, never a later draft input. The prompt may be long and multilingual.

placeholders.prompt: The original natural-language report request, verbatim, isolated for bidirectional text.

shelf_saved.context: Disabled Save button label and announced status when the shown report’s original prompt already exists on this Book’s shared shelf. Keep very short.

shelf_saving.context: Pending label on the disabled Save button and announced status while the original prompt is being saved to this Book’s shared shelf. Keep very short.

shelf_removing.context: Announced pending status under the Book-shared prompt shelf while removing one saved request. The request stays visible until the API confirms removal. Keep very short.

shelf_options.context: Accessible name and tooltip of the small menu button at the end of one Book-shared saved request, in the row just above the report request input. It opens a menu to move the saved request within the row or remove it. The prompt may be long and multilingual.

placeholders.prompt: The original natural-language report request, verbatim, isolated for bidirectional text.

shelf_move_first.context: Item of the small menu of one Book-shared saved request, in the row of saved requests just above the report request input. Moves the request to the start of the row, where the request that opens first when the Book opens sits. Short imperative, like the other items of the menu.

shelf_move_left.context: Item of the small menu of one Book-shared saved request, in the row of saved requests just above the report request input. Moves the request one place to the left on screen. Left is the literal screen direction, never translated as earlier or later: in right-to-left languages it moves the request later in the row. Short imperative.

shelf_move_right.context: Item of the small menu of one Book-shared saved request, in the row of saved requests just above the report request input. Moves the request one place to the right on screen. Right is the literal screen direction, never translated as earlier or later: in right-to-left languages it moves the request earlier in the row. Short imperative.

shelf_moved.context: Announced by screen readers, not shown, after one Book-shared saved request was moved within the row of saved requests above the input. Says where it is now, counting from the start of the row. Keep short.

placeholders.position: The request's place in the row, from 1 at its start, formatted as a number in the language.
placeholders.count: How many saved requests the row holds, formatted as a number in the language.

shelf_move_error.text: Could not move the saved request. Try moving it again.
shelf_move_error.context: Alert under the Book-shared shelf after moving a saved request fails. The saved requests go back to the order they had, and the person can retry safely from its menu or reload the saved requests.

problem_empty_book.text: This Book has no transactions yet, so there's nothing to report.
problem_empty_book.context: Message shown when Report opens a Bkper Book that has no transactions recorded yet, so it can show no report. A Book is a Bkper ledger. One short sentence.

problem_nothing_to_report.text: This Book has nothing to report on: {count} of its {total} accounts with transactions are in no group, and reports read groups.
problem_nothing_to_report.context: Message shown when Report opens a Bkper Book whose Accounts are mostly not organized into Groups (such as Expenses or Assets), so it can show no report: reports are built from Groups. One sentence.

placeholders.count: number of Accounts with transactions that are in no Group, already formatted in the language
placeholders.total: number of Accounts with transactions, already formatted in the language

problem_no_net_result.text: This Book has no net result: no group combines its income and expenses.
problem_no_net_result.context: Message shown when the person asks for the net result (income minus expenses) of a Bkper Book whose Groups give none: no Group holds both its Incoming and its Outgoing Groups. One short sentence.

problem_no_net_result_shared.text: This Book has no net result: its groups {groups} share accounts.
problem_no_net_result_shared.context: Message shown when the person asks for the net result (income minus expenses) of a Bkper Book whose income and expense Groups share Accounts, so they cannot be netted. One short sentence.

placeholders.groups: names of the Groups that share Accounts, verbatim, as a list already joined in the language, such as Sales and Revenue

problem_mixed_group.text: The group {group} holds both balances (assets, liabilities) and activity (income, expenses), so its report would mix them.
problem_mixed_group.context: Message shown when the person asks for the report of a Bkper Group that holds both Asset or Liability Accounts (balances at a date) and Incoming or Outgoing Accounts (income or expenses within a period). One sentence.

problem_ask_owner.text: Ask the Book's owner to organize its groups.
problem_ask_owner.context: Shown after a message about how a Bkper Book's Groups keep it from reports, to a person who may not change the Book's Groups (not its owner or an editor). One short sentence.

problem_ask_owner_start.text: Ask the Book's owner to get started.
problem_ask_owner_start.context: Shown after the message that a Bkper Book has no transactions yet, to a person who may not change the Book (not its owner or an editor): the owner should start recording its transactions. One short sentence.

action_agent_start.context: Button under the message that a Bkper Book has no transactions yet: it opens the Bkper Agent (Bkper's AI assistant, a product name: keep Agent untranslated if the language keeps product names) in the Book to start recording. Keep short.

action_agent_organize.context: Button under a message about how a Bkper Book's Groups keep it from reports: it opens the Bkper Agent (Bkper's AI assistant, a product name: keep Agent untranslated if the language keeps product names) with a request ready to organize the Book's Groups, which the person reads and sends. Keep short.

agent_prompt_nothing_to_report.text: My Book "{book}" has nothing to report on: {count} of its {total} accounts with transactions are in no group. Help me organize them into groups for reports, such as a balance sheet and an income statement. Change groups only, not transactions.
agent_prompt_nothing_to_report.context: Request Report writes for the person into the Bkper Agent's input when their Book's Accounts are mostly in no Group, so it has no reports. The request is written in the person's own voice, for the Bkper Agent (an AI assistant) to read; it ends asking to change Groups only, never transactions.

placeholders.count: number of Accounts with transactions that are in no Group, already formatted in the language
placeholders.total: number of Accounts with transactions, already formatted in the language

agent_prompt_no_net_result.text: My Book "{book}" has no net result: no group combines {incoming} and {outgoing}. Help me organize its groups so income and expenses meet in one group. Change groups only, not transactions.
agent_prompt_no_net_result.context: Request Report writes for the person into the Bkper Agent's input when their Book has no net result: no Group holds both its income Groups and its expense Groups. The request is written in the person's own voice, for the Bkper Agent (an AI assistant) to read; it ends asking to change Groups only, never transactions.

placeholders.incoming: names of the Book's income Groups, verbatim, as a list already joined in the language
placeholders.outgoing: names of the Book's expense Groups, verbatim, as a list already joined in the language

agent_prompt_no_net_result_general.text: My Book "{book}" has no net result: no group combines its income and expenses. Help me organize its groups so income and expenses meet in one group. Change groups only, not transactions.
agent_prompt_no_net_result_general.context: Request Report writes for the person into the Bkper Agent's input when their Book has no net result and lacks income Groups or expense Groups. The request is written in the person's own voice, for the Bkper Agent (an AI assistant) to read; it ends asking to change Groups only, never transactions.

agent_prompt_no_net_result_shared.text: My Book "{book}" has no net result: its groups {shared} share accounts. Help me organize its groups so income and expenses meet in one group. Change groups only, not transactions.
agent_prompt_no_net_result_shared.context: Request Report writes for the person into the Bkper Agent's input when their Book has no net result because its income and expense Groups share Accounts. The request is written in the person's own voice, for the Bkper Agent (an AI assistant) to read; it ends asking to change Groups only, never transactions.

placeholders.shared: names of the Groups that share Accounts, verbatim, as a list already joined in the language

agent_prompt_mixed_group.text: In my Book "{book}", the group {group} combines balances (Asset, Liability) with activity (Incoming, Outgoing). Help me separate them into their own groups. Change groups only, not transactions.
agent_prompt_mixed_group.context: Request Report writes for the person into the Bkper Agent's input when a Group of their Book holds both Asset or Liability Accounts and Incoming or Outgoing Accounts. Asset, Liability, Incoming and Outgoing are Bkper Account types. The request is written in the person's own voice, for the Bkper Agent (an AI assistant) to read; it ends asking to change Groups only, never transactions.
